issues.legal_issue: The dismissal of a partition claim over disputed properties could stand despite the defendant’s contention that his written-statement disclaimer of interest was inseparable from his broader claim that all joint property had been partitioned.
material_facts: The defendant’s written statement asserted that all joint properties had been partitioned and also disclaimed any interest in the properties now in dispute, asserting they had been acquired by other family members from their own resources.
The trial court ordered partition of the plaintiffs’ share in the disputed properties, but the High Court dismissed the partition claim concerning them.
The High Court noted the lack of reliable evidence that the properties had been in joint possession and that the defendant’s name did not appear in the acquisition transactions.
On appeal, the defendant argued that the High Court could not rely on his disclaimer while rejecting his broader assertion of complete partition.
The Supreme Court dismissed the appeal without setting out further reasoning.
issues.conclusion: The appeal was dismissed, leaving undisturbed the dismissal of the partition claim concerning the disputed properties.
issues.legal_principle: The Court cited no statutory provision or earlier case and did not state a broader legal test. It dismissed the challenge to the High Court’s fact-based conclusion, notwithstanding the argument that the written-statement disclaimer had to be read together with the defendant’s claim of complete partition.

rule.if: partition_suit_appeal and written_statement_disclaimed_interest and (joint_possession_not_proved and defendant_not_named_in_acquisitions)

predicates.partition_suit_appeal: The matter is an appeal concerning a claim to partition disputed properties.
predicates.written_statement_disclaimed_interest: The defendant stated in the written statement that he had no interest in the disputed properties.
predicates.joint_possession_not_proved: The court found no reliable evidence that the disputed properties had been in joint possession.
predicates.defendant_not_named_in_acquisitions: The defendant’s name did not appear in the transactions by which the disputed properties were acquired.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerning partition follows a written-statement disclaimer of interest, and joint possession is not proved and the defendant is not named in the acquisitions, the partition claim for the disputed properties remains dismissed.
